messages:
maya: Heads-up: seeing a sudden p95/p99 latency spike (~2-3x) for small-context chat models in eu-west-1 since last night's infra driver rollout (NVIDIA 525 -> 535).
vikram: Same. Throughput dropped on the smallest GPU pools, latency tail moved right. No code deploys on model side.
sebastian: I ran a quick nvprof and triton profiler on staging. Looks like a lot more requests are falling back from FlashAttention -> slower aten kernels. Fallback rate jumped from ~1% to ~22% after the driver bump.
jess: Any error logs from the FlashAttention binaries?
sebastian: Got this from staging logs: 
```
[flash_attn] init: trying kernel variant flash_256_fwd
[flash_attn] kernel check failed: cuBLAS workspace mismatch, falling back
[kernel] selected: aten_attention_fallback (lat 3.6ms) vs flash_attn (0.9ms)
```
maya: Interesting — workspace/cuda runtime incompatibility could be driver-related.
vikram: Also seeing KV cache hit ratio dip during spikes. Investigating if batching/scheduler changes are evicting or bypassing cache.
jess: Did the runtime config change in the rollout? Any heuristics altered?
vikram: Yes — infra changed the gpu-scheduler default to more aggressive preemption to reduce 99.9th latency for long-running jobs: `max_queue_wait_ms: 4` (was 8). That reduced batching aggregation window. More smaller batches -> more kernel selection churn + cache warmup overhead.
maya: Aha — smaller batches can change sequence length distribution and kernel selector heuristics. If FlashAttention selection depends on workspace size or sequence length thresholds, churn could trigger fallback more often.
perf-bot: metric alert: flashattn_fallback_rate (eu-west-1) = 22% (+21pp), p99_latency_chat-small = 320ms (+210ms).
sebastian: Repro steps I used: snapshot model v2 on staging, roll driver -> run synthetic throughput with varied seq lengths: `python perf_driver_test.py --seq 32 --batch 1..8 --duration 5m`
vikram: On repro, driver 535 yields intermittent `cuMemAlloc` warnings during kernel init on heavy churn. Could be driver allocator behavior + our memory pooling assumptions.
jess: Options: (1) rollback driver on affected nodes, (2) force kernel policy to prefer flash kernels unless explicit failure, (3) relax scheduler preemption to restore batching window.
maya: Immediate plan: rollback driver on a small canary of pools tonight, and revert gpu-scheduler max_queue_wait_ms to 8 on those pools. Post-mortem/next steps: add metric for flashattn_fallback_rate and kv_cache_hotset_hit_ratio, and add guard in kernel selector to avoid oscillation.
vikram: I can push the config revert & driver rollback to canary today. Assigning to @vikram.
sebastian: I'll draft a short patch to kernel selector to remember successful kernel for X mins per model+shape to avoid flip-flop.
jess: Add an alert to oncall if fallback_rate > 5% for > 5m.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: rollback-driver -> eu-west-1/canary (3 nodes). ETA 18m.
maya: Thanks. Keep notes in thread, and add perf traces to the incident ticket. :thumbsup:
vikram: Update: rollback complete on canary, fallback_rate back to 1.2%, p99 moved back close to baseline. Pushing config revert next.
sebastian: Filing follow-up PRs for selector sticky policy + better error logging from flash kernels.
jess: Good work. After fixes, we should run a matrix of driver versions + kernel selectors in CI to catch this earlier.
maya: Agreed. Captured action items: rollback + config revert (done for canary), metric + alert, selector sticky policy, CI matrix. Closing for now once canary stable.
perf-bot: incident-note: kernel-selection-regression detected -> triaged to eng-runtime.
